content.text: In regions like Nigeria, Ghana, and Venezuela, digital creators face significant challenges when trying to sell products online. Major platforms such as PayPal and Stripe are often inaccessible, forcing creators to look for alternatives that do not compromise their autonomy. The architecture of digital product stores must adapt to these restrictions, enabling creators to establish their own [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/sovereign-commerce-infrastructure-digital-creators-honest-side-side-19|sovereign]] commerce without relying on traditional [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/usdt-payment-gateways-digital-products-every-detail-you-6|COREMERCH guide to payment]] processors. This is where the idea of a no-KYC payment system comes into play, allowing seamless transactions while retaining [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/complete-deep-dive-solana-payments-digital-products-serious-3|The Complete]] control over the digital store.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: How to Start Selling Digital Products with Crypto Payments at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/full-infrastructure-guide-automated-digital-product-delivery-crypto-3. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: What This Actually Is and Why It Matters: Digital product

A no-KYC payment system provides a foundational solution for digital creators who are often shut out of mainstream payment platforms. By utilizing cryptocurrencies, creators can bypass the stringent identity checks imposed by platforms like PayPal and Stripe. This model not only assures privacy but also minimizes transaction fees significantly. For instance, while Gumroad typically charges 10% on each sale, a no-KYC option like NOWPayments only takes a mere 0.5%. This stark difference translates into substantial retained income, critical for creators in regions with limited financial infrastructure.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

The architecture of a digital product store utilizing no-KYC payments is built on a combination of free and open-source tools. Using platforms like GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, alongside backend solutions such as Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, creators can develop a fully functional online store. Payment processing is handled by NOWPayments, which supports over 300 cryptocurrencies and converts prices in USD at the time of transaction. This setup not only automates product delivery but also ensures that creators maintain complete ownership of their data, a critical aspect of infrastructure sovereignty.
Who This Is Built For and Why

This infrastructure is specifically designed for digital creators in regions that experience financial isolation. Whether you're selling ebooks, courses, templates, or software, this architecture accommodates various digital products while ensuring seamless payment processing without KYC requirements. The goal is to empower creators who have been locked out of existing platforms by providing them with the tools necessary to build, deploy, and manage their own commerce stacks. It serves as a reliable and cost-effective alternative, enabling creators to focus on what they do best—creating.
Retain more of your earnings with low transaction fees using NOWPayments.
The Components That Make It Work Together

The key components of this architecture include hosting, backend logic, order storage, file delivery, and payment processing. GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages serve as the hosting solution, while Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script manage backend logic for order fulfillment. For order storage, options like Supabase or Google Sheets are utilized, allowing creators easy access to their data. File delivery is streamlined through Google Drive or Cloudflare R2, ensuring instant access for customers. Finally, NOWPayments facilitates payment processing, enabling creators to accept cryptocurrency with minimal fees. Together, these components create a robust and efficient digital commerce infrastructure.
How to Use This Knowledge to Deploy Today

To start deploying your own digital product store, begin by selecting a hosting solution like GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages. Next, set up backend logic using Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script to handle order processing. Utilize Supabase or Google Sheets for tracking orders and manage file delivery through Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. Integrate NOWPayments for payment processing, ensuring you can accept a wide range of cryptocurrencies. For those seeking comprehensive guidance, the Complete Builder Kit ($197) provides all six blueprints and seven templates needed to launch your store effectively. Visit https://coremerch.github.io/products.html for more details.
How do I sell an ebook online without PayPal or Stripe?

You can sell an ebook online without PayPal or Stripe by utilizing a no-KYC payment solution like NOWPayments, which processes cryptocurrency transactions. This method allows you to retain full ownership of your store and avoid high fees associated with traditional platforms. By leveraging free tools for hosting and backend logic, you can create a fully operational digital store.
Maintain full control over your data and store without platform dependencies.

If you're looking to sell digital products without relying on conventional platforms, consider the Complete Builder Kit ($197). It includes everything you need to build, deploy, and scale your sovereign digital commerce stack. This solution is tailored for creators in restricted regions, allowing them to thrive independently.
Your Deployment Checklist

Build your product before you build your store — the product is the point, not the infrastructure. Once your product is ready and in delivery-ready format, create your NOWPayments account and configure wallet addresses. Choose Stack 01 for self-deployment following the Blueprint, or Stack 02 for COREMERCH deployment. Upload your product file to Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 and note the file path. Configure the product in your backend with the file path, USD price, and delivery email template. Build your product page on the storefront with clear product description, pricing in USD, and the checkout flow. Run a complete mainnet test. Check that the download link works and expires correctly after the configured time period.
